feedback.problem: Which of the following functions is continuous on the interval $[-1,2]?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The correct answer is the following. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945275/assets/8bfb5e934d6ce86fc478c5ff200db616f65c95956030ccfb247e526551ee8a37.png)

  

Indeed, this function is continuous on the open intervals $(-\infty ,-\sqrt{3}),$ $(-\sqrt{3},2),$ and $(2,6).$

Additionally, the function is left-continuous at $x=2.$ Hence, it is continuous on the interval $(-\sqrt{3},2].$

So, we can say that the function is continuous on the intervals $(-\infty ,\sqrt{3}),$ $(-\sqrt{3},2],$ and $(2,6).$ It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

Therefore, this function is continuous on $[-1,2],$ because $[-1,2]$ is contained inside the interval $(-\sqrt{3},2].$

Notice that:

- $q(x)$ is not left-continuous at $x=2,$ so it is not continuous on the interval $[-1,2].$

- $f(x)$ is not defined at $x=0,$ and so it is not continuous on the interval $[-1,2].$

- $g(x)$ has a removable discontinuity at some point in the interval $(0,2).$  So it is not continuous on the interval $[-1,2].$

- $h(x)$ is not defined at $x=-1,$ and so it is not continuous on the interval $[-1,2].$
